distractors.reason: 'Fluent' is an adjective. We need an adverb to modify the verb 'speak', so we say 'speak fluently'.
'Fluency' is a noun. It cannot modify a verb directly, so we don't say 'speak fluency'.
'Fluid' describes smooth movement or liquids. It is not used as an adverb with 'speak' in this sense.

example_sentence: She can ___ after only two years in Canada.
l1_interference: Os falantes de português costumam colocar o advérbio antes do verbo, dizendo 'fluently speak' em vez de 'speak fluently'. Em inglês, o advérbio vem depois do verbo.
explanation: In English, adverbs of manner usually come after the verb they describe. 'Speak fluently' describes how someone uses the language, so the adverb follows the verb.

related_collocations.example: Please speak clearly so everyone can understand.
He spoke softly so the baby would not wake up.
Listen carefully to the instructions before you start.

memory_tip: VERB first, ADVERB after: speak fluently, listen carefully, work hard | Portuguese order is often adverb first, so check the English order
